literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在稳定状态下,循环 IgG 和 IgA 之间观察到适度的克隆重叠。超过 80% 的抗原特异性单体 IgA 也可检测为二聚体 IgA。相对于单体 IgA 和 IgG,二聚 IgA 以表位特异性方式显着增强中和效力。 [10.1073/pnas.2603905123]
人 诺如病毒 VLP 与猪和狗肠道组织结合并被其内化,其效率分别与猪和犬 诺如病毒 相当。在鸡组织中未检测到人、猪或犬 诺如病毒 的结合或内化。人诺如病毒在猪肠道组织中复制,而动物诺如病毒在人肠道细胞中表现出有限的细胞内摄取。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2713851]
当应用于废水数据时,该模型显示出样本外预测与观察到的跨下水道废水病毒载量之间的一致一致性,并生成了模型推断的跨疾病分区的时间感染动态。 [10.1021/acs.est.6c02418]
包括 GII.2、GII.3 和 GII.6 在内的基因型几十年来保持相对稳定,但仍占疾病的很大一部分。在 GII 中,快速进化的谱系(例如 GII.4)和偶尔出现的基因型(例如 GII.17)(由衣壳抗原漂移和新型开放阅读框 1/开放阅读框 2 (ORF1/ORF2) 重组体驱动)表现出频繁的适应和多洲扩张。 [10.20935/acadimmunodis8443]
诺如病毒 感染的总体 患病率 为 44%,其中 GII (73%) 超过 GI (18%)。9% 的病例检测到胃肠道/胃肠道双重感染。临床上,80% 的病例报告发烧,86% 的大便频率增加,所有参与者 (100%) 都观察到脱水。 [10.5897/jgmv2026.0086]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: A modest clonal overlap was observed between circulating IgG and IgA at steady state. More than 80% of antigen-specific monomeric IgA was also detectable as dimeric IgA. Dimeric IgA markedly enhanced neutralization potency relative to monomeric IgA and IgG in an epitope-specific manner. [10.1073/pnas.2603905123]

Human norovirus VLPs bound to and were internalized by pig and dog intestinal tissue with efficiency comparable to porcine and canine noroviruses, respectively. No binding or internalization of human, porcine, or canine noroviruses was detected in chicken tissue. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2713851]

When applied to wastewater data, the model showed consistent agreement between out-of-sample predictions and observed wastewater viral load across sewersheds and generated model-inferred temporal infection dynamics across disease compartments. [10.1021/acs.est.6c02418]
Genotypes including GII.2, GII.3, and GII.6 remain relatively stable over decades yet continue to account for a substantial proportion of disease. [10.20935/acadimmunodis8443]

The overall prevalence of norovirus infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). [10.5897/jgmv2026.0086]

news.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 医生注意到病毒性胃部感染的增加,尤其是类似 诺如病毒 的疾病,这些疾病在拥挤的空间中迅速传播。这是《德干纪事报》报道的一般性观察,而不是经过证实的 暴发。 [news-bff7f86479a36cb5]
德国电子音乐节上的 诺如病毒 暴发 被讨论为英国音乐节的潜在灾难场景。 [news-0a037f6dc8b1ecf7]
公主邮轮红宝石公主号上发生的一起 诺如病毒 暴发 事故导致 125 人患病,这是该邮轮公司 2026 年发生的第三起此类事件 (N1)。CDC确认了暴发,公主邮轮表示,有限数量的客人报告有轻度胃肠道疾病(N6)。 [news-132397de41bade9f]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: Doctors are noticing a rise in viral stomach infections, particularly norovirus-like illnesses that spread rapidly in crowded spaces. This is reported by the Deccan Chronicle as a general observation, not a confirmed outbreak. [news-bff7f86479a36cb5]
Norovirus outbreak at a German electronic festival, discussed as a potential disaster scenario for UK festivals. [news-0a037f6dc8b1ecf7]

A norovirus outbreak sickened 125 people aboard the Princess Cruises ship Ruby Princess, marking the cruise line’s third such incident in 2026 (N1). The CDC confirmed the outbreak, and Princess Cruises stated that a limited number of guests reported mild gastrointestinal illness (N6). [news-132397de41bade9f]

papers.title: Antiviral strategies against human norovirus: Molecular targets, therapeutics, and vaccine development.
papers.abstract: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide and represents a major unmet challenge in antiviral drug and vaccine development. HuNoV is a non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA virus characterized by extensive genetic diversity and rapid evolution, which contribute to recurrent outbreaks in the absence of effective licensed therapeutics. Despite substantial progress in understanding HuNoV molecular biology, effective antiviral strategies remain limited, in part due to historical limitations in experimental model systems and the virus's ability to evade host antiviral responses. Recent advances in HuNoV in vitro culture systems, particularly human intestinal enteroids, and inhibitor screening platforms have improved the identification of antiviral candidates, while parallel efforts in vaccine development have yielded immunogenicity data in preclinical and early-stage clinical studies. However, significant challenges persist, including antigenic diversity, strain-specific immunity, and limited correlates of protection. This review provides a critical analysis of the molecular mechanisms governing HuNoV infection, immune evasion, and replication, with a focused emphasis on key antiviral targets, inhibitory strategies, and therapeutic development. Moreover, this review outlines key limitations and future directions for the development of effective therapeutic and preventive measures against HuNoV infection.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human norovirus (HuNoV), a non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA virus, as the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis globally, focusing on its molecular targets, antiviral therapeutics, and vaccine development strategies within human populations. The central question addresses the unmet need for effective antiviral drugs and vaccines despite substantial progress in understanding HuNoV molecular biology and replication mechanisms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on HuNoV antiviral strategies without reporting databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts. It relies on critical analysis of molecular mechanisms, immune evasion, and replication, emphasizing key antiviral targets and therapeutic development based on available literature.

papers.title_zh: 针对人类 诺如病毒 的 抗病毒药物 策略:分子靶点、治疗方法和 疫苗 开发。
papers.source_body_en: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide and represents a major unmet challenge in antiviral drug and vaccine development. HuNoV is a non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA virus characterized by extensive genetic diversity and rapid evolution, which contribute to recurrent outbreaks in the absence of effective licensed therapeutics. Despite substantial progress in understanding HuNoV molecular biology, effective antiviral strategies remain limited, in part due to historical limitations in experimental model systems and the virus's ability to evade host antiviral responses. Recent advances in HuNoV in vitro culture systems, particularly human intestinal enteroids, and inhibitor screening platforms have improved the identification of antiviral candidates, while parallel efforts in vaccine development have yielded immunogenicity data in preclinical and early-stage clinical studies. However, significant challenges persist, including antigenic diversity, strain-specific immunity, and limited correlates of protection. This review provides a critical analysis of the molecular mechanisms governing HuNoV infection, immune evasion, and replication, with a focused emphasis on key antiviral targets, inhibitory strategies, and therapeutic development. Moreover, this review outlines key limitations and future directions for the development of effective therapeutic and preventive measures against HuNoV infection.

papers.title: Norovirus inter-species transmission in an ex vivo model is dependent on virus internalization capacity.
papers.abstract: Human noroviruses (HuNoV) are the most common cause of viral gastroenteritis worldwide, causing sporadic cases and outbreaks. Noroviruses that infect wild and domestic animals, including pigs and dogs, are genetically related to human noroviruses, increasing the potential for cross-species transmission. To investigate the potential of noroviruses to cross the species barrier, we used porcine, canine, and avian precision-cut intestinal slices. We show that human norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) bind to pig and dog intestinal tissue and are taken up with a similar efficiency as the porcine and canine noroviruses, respectively. In contrast, no binding or internalization of human, porcine, or canine noroviruses was detected in chicken tissue. We further showed that human norovirus replicates in pig intestinal tissue. In contrast, while animal noroviruses attached to human intestinal cells, intracellular uptake was limited. This suggests that human-to-animal transmission is more likely than animal-to-human transmission and that viral uptake likely presents a species barrier.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human noroviruses (HuNoV) are the leading cause of viral gastroenteritis globally, yet the potential for cross-species transmission remains poorly understood. analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used precision-cut intestinal slices from pigs, dogs, and chickens to model inter-species transmission of noroviruses. Porcine, canine, and avian tissues were exposed to human, porcine, and canine noroviruses to assess binding and internalization.
analysis.methods: Porcine, canine, and avian precision-cut intestinal slices were incubated with human norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs), porcine norovirus, and canine norovirus to evaluate binding and internalization efficiency. Replication of human norovirus in pig intestinal tissue was assessed.
analysis.main_results: Human norovirus VLPs bound to and were internalized by pig and dog intestinal tissue with efficiency comparable to porcine and canine noroviruses, respectively. No binding or internalization of human, porcine, or canine noroviruses was detected in chicken tissue. Human norovirus replicated in pig intestinal tissue, whereas animal noroviruses showed limited intracellular uptake in human intestinal cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that human-to-animal transmission may be more likely than animal-to-human transmission, with viral uptake acting as a species barrier. This is the first demonstration of human norovirus replication in porcine intestinal tissue ex vivo.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results imply that pigs could serve as reservoirs for human norovirus, raising concerns for zoonotic spillover and food safety. The study highlights the need for surveillance of animal hosts in norovirus-endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The ex vivo model may not fully replicate in vivo conditions, limiting generalizability to natural infections. The evidence is moderate due to the absence of in vivo validation and small sample size in the experimental setup.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential for noroviruses to cross species barriers using precision-cut intestinal slices from pigs, dogs, and chickens. Human norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) bound to and were internalized by pig and dog tissues as efficiently as animal noroviruses, while no interaction was observed in chicken tissue. Human norovirus replicated in porcine intestinal tissue, whereas animal noroviruses showed limited uptake in human cells. The findings suggest human-to-animal transmission may be more likely than the reverse, with viral uptake acting as a species barrier. This is the first ex vivo demonstration of human norovirus replication in pig tissue, underscoring the need for surveillance of animal reservoirs to assess zoonotic risk.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用猪、狗和鸡的精密切割肠道切片来模拟 诺如病毒 的种间 传播。将猪、犬和禽组织暴露于人、猪和犬 诺如病毒 以评估结合和内化。
elements_zh.methods: 将猪、犬和禽类精密切割的肠道切片与人 诺如病毒 病毒样颗粒 (VLP)、猪 诺如病毒 和犬 诺如病毒 一起孵育,以评估结合和内化效率。评估了人 诺如病毒 在猪肠道组织中的复制。
elements_zh.main_results: 人 诺如病毒 VLP 与猪和狗肠道组织结合并被其内化,其效率分别与猪和犬 诺如病毒 相当。在鸡组织中未检测到人、猪或犬 诺如病毒 的结合或内化。人诺如病毒在猪肠道组织中复制,而动物诺如病毒在人肠道细胞中表现出有限的细胞内摄取。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,人与动物之间的 传播 可能比动物与人之间的 传播 更有可能,病毒摄取起到了物种屏障的作用。这是人类 诺如病毒 在离体猪肠道组织中复制的首次演示。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,猪可以充当人类 诺如病毒 的 储存宿主,引起人们对人畜共患 跨物种溢出 和食品安全的担忧。该研究强调了 诺如病毒 流行地区对动物 宿主 的 监测 的需求。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 离体模型可能无法完全复制体内条件,限制了自然感染的普遍性。由于缺乏体内验证且实验设置中样本量较小,证据不充分。

Human norovirus replicated in pig intestinal tissue, whereas animal noroviruses showed limited intracellular uptake in human intestinal cells.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that human-to-animal transmission may be more likely than animal-to-human transmission, with viral uptake acting as a species barrier. This is the first demonstration of human norovirus replication in porcine intestinal tissue ex vivo.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results imply that pigs could serve as reservoirs for human norovirus, raising concerns for zoonotic spillover and food safety. The study highlights the need for surveillance of animal hosts in norovirus-endemic regions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The ex vivo model may not fully replicate in vivo conditions, limiting generalizability to natural infections. The evidence is moderate due to the absence of in vivo validation and small sample size in the experimental setup.

papers.title_zh: 离体模型中的 诺如病毒 种间 传播 取决于病毒内化能力。
papers.source_body_en: Human noroviruses (HuNoV) are the most common cause of viral gastroenteritis worldwide, causing sporadic cases and outbreaks. Noroviruses that infect wild and domestic animals, including pigs and dogs, are genetically related to human noroviruses, increasing the potential for cross-species transmission. To investigate the potential of noroviruses to cross the species barrier, we used porcine, canine, and avian precision-cut intestinal slices. We show that human norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) bind to pig and dog intestinal tissue and are taken up with a similar efficiency as the porcine and canine noroviruses, respectively. In contrast, no binding or internalization of human, porcine, or canine noroviruses was detected in chicken tissue. We further showed that human norovirus replicates in pig intestinal tissue. In contrast, while animal noroviruses attached to human intestinal cells, intracellular uptake was limited. This suggests that human-to-animal transmission is more likely than animal-to-human transmission and that viral uptake likely presents a species barrier.

papers.title: Serum IgA proteomics reveals clonal composition and neutralization of dimeric and monomeric IgA repertoires against human norovirus.
papers.abstract: Protection against human norovirus correlates with attachment ligand blockade antibody titers, fecal IgA titers, and serum IgA titers. IgA responses in serum comprise approximately 80 to 95% of monomeric IgA (mIgA) and 5 to 20% of dimeric IgA (dIgA). Using serum LC-MS/MS proteomics, we established clonal relationships between circulating IgG and IgA, as well as between dIgA and mIgA. We observed a modest degree of clonal overlap between circulating IgG and IgA at steady state and found that more than 80% of antigen-specific mIgA was also detectable as dIgA. We biochemically characterized neutralizing epitopes on norovirus GII.4 virus-like particles (VLPs) targeted by serum IgA clonotypes and demonstrated that dIgA markedly enhances neutralization potency relative to mIgA and IgG in an epitope-specific manner. Cryoelectron microscopy and cryoelectron tomography revealed that whether IgA dimerization enhances viral neutralization depends on epitope accessibility on the VLP and antibody binding orientation. Together, these findings provide molecular-level resolution of the serum IgA response and define the structural basis by which dIgA enhances neutralization potency in an epitope-specific manner.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title_original: Serum IgA proteomics reveals clonal composition and neutralization of dimeric and monomeric IgA repertoires against human norovirus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed why serum IgA responses against human norovirus remain incompletely understood despite their likely role in protection. It aimed to resolve how clonal composition and structural features of dimeric versus monomeric IgA repertoires relate to neutralization.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors used serum LC-MS/MS proteomics to establish clonal relationships among circulating IgG, IgA, and between dimeric and monomeric IgA. They characterized neutralizing epitopes on norovirus GII.4 virus-like particles (VLPs) targeted by serum IgA clonotypes.
analysis.methods: Serum IgA clonotypes were identified and compared using LC-MS/MS proteomics to assess clonal overlap between IgG and IgA and between dIgA and mIgA. Neutralization potency of dIgA, mIgA, and IgG was measured against GII.4 VLPs. Cryoelectron microscopy and cryoelectron tomography were used to visualize epitope accessibility and antibody binding orientation.
analysis.main_results: A modest clonal overlap was observed between circulating IgG and IgA at steady state. More than 80% of antigen-specific monomeric IgA was also detectable as dimeric IgA. Dimeric IgA markedly enhanced neutralization potency relative to monomeric IgA and IgG in an epitope-specific manner.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide molecular-level resolution of the serum IgA response and define the structural basis by which dimeric IgA enhances neutralization potency in an epitope-specific manner. This contrasts with monomeric IgA and IgG, highlighting a previously unappreciated role of IgA dimerization.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that dimeric IgA may be a more effective target for norovirus vaccine design and serological assays than monomeric IgA or IgG. They also imply that epitope accessibility and binding orientation are critical determinants of neutralization efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on virus-like particles rather than live virus, which may not fully recapitulate natural infection dynamics. The generalizability of findings to broader norovirus genotypes or clinical settings remains to be established, warranting further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study used serum LC-MS/MS proteomics to map clonal relationships among circulating IgG, IgA, and between dimeric and monomeric IgA in human norovirus immunity. It found that over 80% of antigen-specific monomeric IgA is also present as dimeric IgA and that dimeric IgA exhibits markedly enhanced neutralization potency against GII.4 virus-like particles compared to monomeric IgA and IgG, with effects dependent on epitope accessibility and antibody binding orientation. papers.source_body_en: Protection against human norovirus correlates with attachment ligand blockade antibody titers, fecal IgA titers, and serum IgA titers. IgA responses in serum comprise approximately 80 to 95% of monomeric IgA (mIgA) and 5 to 20% of dimeric IgA (dIgA). Using serum LC-MS/MS proteomics, we established clonal relationships between circulating IgG and IgA, as well as between dIgA and mIgA. We observed a modest degree of clonal overlap between circulating IgG and IgA at steady state and found that more than 80% of antigen-specific mIgA was also detectable as dIgA. We biochemically characterized neutralizing epitopes on norovirus GII.4 virus-like particles (VLPs) targeted by serum IgA clonotypes and demonstrated that dIgA markedly enhances neutralization potency relative to mIgA and IgG in an epitope-specific manner. Cryoelectron microscopy and cryoelectron tomography revealed that whether IgA dimerization enhances viral neutralization depends on epitope accessibility on the VLP and antibody binding orientation. Together, these findings provide molecular-level resolution of the serum IgA response and define the structural basis by which dIgA enhances neutralization potency in an epitope-specific manner.

papers.title: Treatment With Ruxolitinib and TAK-779 Enhances GII.17 Human Norovirus Replication and Enables Serial Passaging in Human Intestinal Enteroids.
papers.abstract: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high-titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies. Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication. Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib-a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor-and TAK-779-a C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C-C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist-on HuNoV replication in wild-type jejunal HIEs. TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control. In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication. Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0- and 10.7-fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging. These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.

papers.title_zh: 治疗 与 Ruxolitinib 和 TAK-779 一起增强 GII.17 人类 诺如病毒 复制并实现人肠肠类的连续传代。
papers.source_body_en: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high-titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies. Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication. Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib-a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor-and TAK-779-a C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C-C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist-on HuNoV replication in wild-type jejunal HIEs. TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control. In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication. Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0- and 10.7-fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging. These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.

papers.title: Genetic evolution and vaccine challenges in norovirus genogroup II infection
papers.abstract: Norovirus genogroup II (GII) is the most common etiology of acute gastroenteritis on a global level, and this is due to a significant degree of genetic heterogeneity, rapid adaptive evolution, and extremely efficient person-to-person and environmental transmission systems. Within GII, rapidly evolving lineages such as GII.4 and episodically emerging genotypes like GII.17 (driven by capsid antigenic drift and novel open reading frame 1/open reading frame 2 (ORF1/ORF2) recombinants) exhibit frequent adaptation and multi-continent expansion. Genotypes including GII.2, GII.3, and GII.6 remain relatively stable over decades yet continue to account for a substantial proportion of disease. This review combines current evidence on the evolutionary dynamics of norovirus GII, which defines the patterns of genotype replacement, the recombination mechanisms between ORF1 and ORF2, and the structural factors of antigenic variability that contribute to immune evasion and determine the epidemiology in the world. We also review advances in diagnostics, including reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), digital PCR, new isothermal amplification, biosensor platforms, and wastewater surveillance, which are collectively sensitive and more accurate in quantification, and in real-time monitoring in the clinical, food safety, and environmental fields. We also discuss the modern situation in vaccine development, including the use of virus-like particle preparations, messenger RNA (mRNA)-based strategies, and oral adenoviral vectors, their antigenic compositions, key clinical milestones, and the ongoing challenges of lack of robust correlates of protection and overall cross-genotype protection. Key gaps remain in understanding, requiring focused research and policy efforts to improve vaccines and control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the genetic evolution and vaccine challenges associated with norovirus genogroup II (GII) infection. It highlights the global prevalence of GII as a major cause of acute gastroenteritis, driven by its genetic heterogeneity, rapid evolution, and efficient transmission. The review discusses the stability of certain GII genotypes like GII.2, GII.3, and GII.6, while emphasizing the dynamic nature of GII.4 and GII.17 lineages, which undergo antigenic drift and recombination. It also outlines the current state of vaccine development, including virus-like particle preparations, mRNA-based strategies, and oral adenoviral vectors, and identifies key challenges such as the lack of robust correlates of protection and cross-genotype efficacy. The review further explores advances in diagnostic methods, including RT-qPCR, digital PCR, isothermal amplification, biosensor platforms, and wastewater surveillance, which offer improved sensitivity and accuracy. Despite these insights, the review notes significant gaps in understanding that require targeted research and policy efforts to enhance vaccine effectiveness and control strategies.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇综述结合了 诺如病毒 GII 进化动力学的最新证据,定义了基因型替换的模式、ORF1 和 ORF2 之间的重组机制,以及有助于免疫逃避和确定世界上 流行病学 的抗原变异的结构因素。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 包括 GII.2、GII.3 和 GII.6 在内的基因型几十年来保持相对稳定,但仍占疾病的很大一部分。在 GII 中,快速进化的谱系(例如 GII.4)和偶尔出现的基因型(例如 GII.17)(由衣壳抗原漂移和新型开放阅读框 1/开放阅读框 2 (ORF1/ORF2) 重组体驱动)表现出频繁的适应和多洲扩张。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 理解方面仍存在关键差距,需要集中研究和政策努力来改进 疫苗 和控制策略。

papers.title: Viral gastroenteritis: Molecular epidemiology of human norovirus by RT-PCR at University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of Congo
papers.abstract: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.
papers.journal: Journal of General and Molecular Virology

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the molecular epidemiology of human norovirus among children with acute gastroenteritis in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. Conducted as a descriptive cross-sectional study from June to November 2020, it enrolled 50 children aged 28 days to 17 years, with 80% aged ≤5 years. Using RT-PCR, the overall norovirus prevalence was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%) and 9% exhibiting GI/GII co-infections. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2020 年 6 月至 11 月在布拉柴维尔大学医院中心进行了一项描述性横断面研究。招募了 50 名年龄在 28 天至 17 岁之间、患有 AGE 的儿童。百分之八十的年龄≤5 岁。
elements_zh.methods: 使用实时逆转录聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 分析粪便样本,以检测病毒 RNA 并区分 GI 和 GII 基因组。
elements_zh.main_results: 诺如病毒 感染的总体 患病率 为 44%,其中 GII (73%) 超过 GI (18%)。9% 的病例检测到胃肠道/胃肠道双重感染。临床上,80% 的病例报告发烧,86% 的大便频率增加,所有参与者 (100%) 都观察到脱水。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 诺如病毒 是布拉柴维尔儿童 AGE 的一个重要原因。年龄和 诺如病毒 基因组分布之间存在显着相关性 (p = 0.03),其中 GII 在 ≤5 岁儿童中更为普遍。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 建议将分子诊断方法纳入国家 监测 计划并加强卫生措施,以改进预防和控制策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的小样本量和单中心设计限制了普遍性,并且缺乏对照组限制了因果推断。由于这些限制,证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.title_zh: 病毒性胃肠炎:在刚果共和国布拉柴维尔大学医院中心通过 RT-PCR 检测人 流行病学 分子 流行病学
papers.source_body_en: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.

papers.title: A Wastewater-based Modeling Framework for Inferring Norovirus Transmission Dynamics
papers.abstract: Abstract Norovirus is a leading cause of gastroenteritis globally, yet its true infection burden in the community remains poorly understood because of widespread asymptomatic transmission and underreporting. Wastewater-based surveillance is a promising approach for tracking infection trends, but methods for mechanistically linking wastewater viral concentrations to infection dynamics remain limited. Here, we developed a mechanistic SEIR-V framework to infer community-level norovirus transmission dynamics from wastewater data by jointly modeling disease transmission, viral-shedding kinetics, and wastewater viral load. We leveraged temporal fecal shedding data from a controlled human challenge study and systematic literature review to parametrize symptom-specific shedding profiles and integrate them into the framework. Applied to wastewater data from four treatment plants in El Paso, Texas, the model showed consistent agreement between out-of-sample predictions and observed wastewater viral load across sewersheds while generating model-inferred temporal infection dynamics across disease compartments. Sensitivity analysis further showed that wastewater viral load was influenced by transmission, shedding, and viral loss parameters, whereas inferred infection dynamics were primarily influenced by the transmission rate and infectious duration. This work provides a mechanistic wastewater modeling framework to infer norovirus transmission dynamics and could support proactive public health surveillance, particularly for pathogens with high asymptomatic transmission and limited clinical reporting.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus causes substantial global gastroenteritis burden, but its true community infection dynamics are obscured by asymptomatic transmission and underreporting, creating a need for improved surveillance methods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a mechanistic SEIR-V modeling framework to infer community-level norovirus transmission dynamics from wastewater data collected at four treatment plants in El Paso, Texas.
analysis.methods: The framework jointly modeled disease transmission, viral-shedding kinetics, and wastewater viral load, using temporal fecal shedding data from a controlled human challenge study and a systematic literature review to parametrize symptom-specific shedding profiles.
analysis.main_results: When applied to wastewater data, the model showed consistent agreement between out-of-sample predictions and observed wastewater viral load across sewersheds and generated model-inferred temporal infection dynamics across disease compartments.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating that wastewater viral load is influenced by transmission, shedding, and viral loss parameters, while inferred infection dynamics are primarily driven by the transmission rate and infectious duration, representing a novel mechanistic approach to linking wastewater data to infection dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This framework could support proactive public health surveillance for pathogens with high asymptomatic transmission and limited clinical reporting by enabling inference of community infection dynamics from wastewater measurements.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on wastewater data from a single geographic region and the need for external validation across diverse settings, despite the mechanistic integration of shedding and transmission parameters.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a mechanistic SEIR-V modeling framework that integrates wastewater viral load data with disease transmission and viral-shedding kinetics to infer community-level norovirus infection dynamics. Using fecal shedding profiles from controlled human challenge studies and literature synthesis, the authors parametrized a model applied to wastewater data from four treatment plants in El Paso, Texas. The model accurately predicted observed wastewater viral loads out-of-sample and generated compartmental infection dynamics, with sensitivity analyses indicating that wastewater viral load is influenced by transmission, shedding, and viral loss parameters, while infection dynamics are primarily driven by transmission rate and infectious duration. The framework is positioned as a novel approach to address the underestimation of norovirus burden due to asymptomatic transmission and underreporting, offering potential for proactive public health surveillance.

elements_zh.methods: 该框架使用来自受控人类挑战研究的时间粪便排泄数据和系统文献综述来对疾病 传播、病毒排泄动力学和废水病毒载量进行联合建模,以参数化特定症状的排泄概况。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 诺如病毒 是全球胃肠炎的主要原因,但由于广泛存在无症状 传播 和漏报,其在社区中的真实感染负担仍知之甚少。基于废水的 监测 是追踪感染趋势的一种有前途的方法,但从机械上将废水病毒浓度与感染动态联系起来的方法仍然有限。在这里,我们开发了一个机械 SEIR-V 框架,通过联合建模疾病 传播、病毒脱落动力学和废水病毒载量,从废水数据推断社区级 诺如病毒 传播 动态。我们利用来自受控人类挑战研究和系统文献综述的时间粪便排泄数据来参数化特定症状的排泄概况并将其整合到框架中。该模型应用于德克萨斯州埃尔帕索四家 治疗 工厂的废水数据,显示出样本外预测与下水道中观察到的废水病毒载量之间的一致性,同时生成了模型推断的跨疾病分区的时间感染动态。敏感性分析进一步表明,废水病毒载量受 传播、脱落和病毒损失参数的影响,而推断的感染动态主要受 传播 率和感染持续时间的影响。这项工作提供了一个机械废水建模框架来推断 诺如病毒 传播 动态,并可以支持积极主动的公共卫生 监测,特别是对于无症状 传播 和临床报告有限的病原体。

analysis_zh.methods: 该框架使用来自受控人类挑战研究的时间粪便排泄数据和系统文献综述来对疾病 传播、病毒排泄动力学和废水病毒载量进行联合建模,以参数化特定症状的排泄概况。
analysis_zh.main_results: 当应用于废水数据时,该模型显示出样本外预测与观察到的跨下水道废水病毒载量之间的一致一致性,并生成了模型推断的跨疾病分区的时间感染动态。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管脱落和 传播 参数进行了机械整合,但由于依赖于单一地理区域的废水数据以及需要在不同环境下进行外部验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Microbial assessment of recontamination with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter in patient room environment in a burn unit.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Numerous studies have demonstrated that environmental contamination with several epidemiologically important pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp, Acinetobacter, norovirus, and Clostridioides difficile, can persist for several days to months and contributes to the transmission of these pathogens. METHODS: This study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to determine the time to recontamination of environmental surfaces with a multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection. After disinfection, samples were taken from 6 environmental sites using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours. RESULTS: Time to recontamination with Acinetobacter was as follows: chair, 3 hours; overbed table, 2 hours; stock cabinet, 3 hours; and IV pump, 2 hours. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated that recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly at environmental sites in burn units even after cleaning/disinfection and underscored the need for enhanced environmental cleaning, including continuous disinfection methods, to prevent transmission of health care-associated pathogens.

analysis.main_results: Time to recontamination with Acinetobacter was observed at 2 hours for the overbed table and IV pump, and at 3 hours for the chair and stock cabinet.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly at environmental sites in burn units even after cleaning/disinfection, highlighting the need for enhanced environmental cleaning and continuous disinfection methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the rapidity of environmental recontamination with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in a burn intensive care unit after disinfection. Sampling from six environmental sites using Rodac plates at hourly intervals for 10 hours showed recontamination within 2 to 3 hours at multiple surfaces, including the overbed table, IV pump, chair, and stock cabinet. The authors interpreted these results as evidence that recontamination occurs quickly even after cleaning, emphasizing the need for enhanced and continuous disinfection to prevent healthcare-associated transmission. The study was confined to a single burn unit and a brief observation window, limiting broader applicability.

papers.title: Evolution, diversity and distribution of human Noroviruses:From single hosts to global patterns
papers.abstract: Norovirus, a member of the Caliciviridae family, is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, affecting all age groups and causing substantial morbidity and mortality. Children in developing countries, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly affected. Currently, no specific antivirals or vaccines are licensed for norovirus treatment or prevention. Therapeutic development is complicated by the virus's high diversity, with more than 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, some of which, such as GII.4, continuously generate new antigenic variants. However, the emergence of norovirus diversity, the relationship between within-host and community-level evolution, and the association between viral diversity and treatment outcome remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this thesis aims to improve our understanding of norovirus evolution and epidemiology by addressing two main topics: norovirus diversity and evolution in different hosts, and the use of wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level.

papers.title: How water quality under extreme floods compromises ecosystem services, sanitation and One Health
papers.abstract: In May 2024, Porto Alegre, Brazil, experienced the most intense large-scale precipitation event recorded in the country, exposing major vulnerabilities in flood-protection and sanitation infrastructure. Using high-resolution spatial sampling across 92 sites during the flood peak, we investigated physicochemical parameters, microbiological indicators, ecotoxicity, antibiotic resistance genes, and pathogenic viruses in floodwaters. An integrated analytical framework combined standardized physicochemical analyses, culture-based microbial quantification with antibiotic susceptibility testing, molecular detection of resistance genes and pathogenic viruses by qPCR/RT-PCR, ecotoxicological assays, and principal component analysis to identify contamination pathways and associated environmental and public health risks. Results revealed severe water quality degradation, with turbidity exceeding 470 NTU, mean total phosphorus reaching 1.07 mg/L (21× the legal limit), and mean ammoniacal nitrogen reaching 12.74 mg/L (3.4× the legal limit). coli concentrations exceeded U.S. EPA Recreational Water Quality Criteria by more than one order of magnitude, indicating severe fecal contamination. Ecotoxicity assays using Daphnia magna indicated acute toxicity in stagnant floodwaters. Microbiological analyses detected multidrug-resistant bacteria, with carbapenemase genes ( bla KPC and bla NDM ) widely detected across flooded urban zones, including hospital-adjacent areas. Pathogenic viruses, including Norovirus GI and GII, and Hepatitis A and E, were also detected. Water quality deterioration contributed to the shutdown of five of six drinking water treatment plants, depriving 1.23 million residents of potable water, while wastewater system failures discharged approximately 50,000 m3/day of raw sewage into flooded neighborhoods and the Jacuí River. Unlike most flood studies, this study provides quantitative and in situ evidence collected during the flood peak. By integrating real-time environmental, microbiological, molecular, and ecotoxicological indicators, the proposed framework offers a replicable approach for water quality assessment, risk evaluation, and urban water management under extreme flood conditions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Extreme flooding events can overwhelm sanitation and water-treatment systems, creating conditions that may facilitate the spread of waterborne pathogens such as norovirus. The study was motivated by the unprecedented May 2024 flood in Porto Alegre, Brazil, which exposed critical vulnerabilities in flood-protection and sanitation infrastructure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed high-resolution spatial sampling across 92 sites during the flood peak in Porto Alegre, Brazil, integrating physicochemical, microbiological, molecular, and ecotoxicological analyses to assess contamination pathways and public health risks.
analysis.methods: An integrated analytical framework combined standardized physicochemical analyses, culture-based microbial quantification with antibiotic susceptibility testing, molecular detection of resistance genes and pathogenic viruses by qPCR/RT-PCR, ecotoxicological assays using Daphnia magna, and principal component analysis to identify contamination pathways.
analysis.main_results: Pathogenic viruses, including Norovirus GI and GII, were detected in floodwaters, alongside severe physicochemical degradation (e.g., turbidity >470 NTU, total phosphorus 1.07 mg/L, ammoniacal nitrogen 12.74 mg/L) and high fecal contamination indicated by Escherichia coli concentrations exceeding U.S. EPA Recreational Water Quality Criteria by more than one order of magnitude.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides in situ, quantitative evidence collected during the flood peak, demonstrating that extreme flooding compromises water quality and facilitates the presence of waterborne pathogens such as norovirus. The integrated framework offers a replicable approach for assessing risks under extreme flood conditions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the urgent need for improved flood-resilient water and sanitation infrastructure to mitigate pathogen dissemination during extreme weather events. The shutdown of five of six drinking water treatment plants and discharge of raw sewage into urban zones underscore the public health consequences of such events.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single extreme event in one geographic location, which may restrict generalizability to other flood scenarios or regions. papers.title_zh: 极端洪水下的水质如何损害生态系统服务、卫生和统一健康
papers.source_body_en: In May 2024, Porto Alegre, Brazil, experienced the most intense large-scale precipitation event recorded in the country, exposing major vulnerabilities in flood-protection and sanitation infrastructure. Using high-resolution spatial sampling across 92 sites during the flood peak, we investigated physicochemical parameters, microbiological indicators, ecotoxicity, antibiotic resistance genes, and pathogenic viruses in floodwaters. An integrated analytical framework combined standardized physicochemical analyses, culture-based microbial quantification with antibiotic susceptibility testing, molecular detection of resistance genes and pathogenic viruses by qPCR/RT-PCR, ecotoxicological assays, and principal component analysis to identify contamination pathways and associated environmental and public health risks. Results revealed severe water quality degradation, with turbidity exceeding 470 NTU, mean total phosphorus reaching 1.07 mg/L (21× the legal limit), and mean ammoniacal nitrogen reaching 12.74 mg/L (3.4× the legal limit). coli concentrations exceeded U.S. EPA Recreational Water Quality Criteria by more than one order of magnitude, indicating severe fecal contamination. Ecotoxicity assays using Daphnia magna indicated acute toxicity in stagnant floodwaters. Microbiological analyses detected multidrug-resistant bacteria, with carbapenemase genes ( bla KPC and bla NDM ) widely detected across flooded urban zones, including hospital-adjacent areas. Pathogenic viruses, including Norovirus GI and GII, and Hepatitis A and E, were also detected. Water quality deterioration contributed to the shutdown of five of six drinking water treatment plants, depriving 1.23 million residents of potable water, while wastewater system failures discharged approximately 50,000 m3/day of raw sewage into flooded neighborhoods and the Jacuí River. Unlike most flood studies, this study provides quantitative and in situ evidence collected during the flood peak. By integrating real-time environmental, microbiological, molecular, and ecotoxicological indicators, the proposed framework offers a replicable approach for water quality assessment, risk evaluation, and urban water management under extreme flood conditions.

news.content: Top Tuesday , 18 August 2026 e-Paper Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process Home South Andhra Pradesh Telangana Tamil Nadu Karnataka Keralam Nation Youth World NRI Entertainment Sholay Tollywood Bollywood Sandalwood Kollywood Mollywood Hollywood Movie Reviews Television Music Theatre OTT Sports Cricket Football Tennis Others AI Videos Opinion and Editorials Columns DC Comments Business Environment Technology Youth Queer Beat Education Hyderabad Chronicle DC Decaf Featured Astroguide More Home South Andhra Pradesh Telangana Tamil Nadu Karnataka Keralam Nation Youth World NRI Entertainment Sholay Tollywood Bollywood Sandalwood Kollywood Mollywood Hollywood Movie Reviews Television Music Theatre OTT Sports Cricket Football Tennis Others AI Videos Opinion and Editorials Columns DC Comments Business Environment Technology Youth Queer Beat Education Hyderabad Chronicle DC Decaf Featured Astroguide Home Just In South Andhra Pradesh Telangana Tamil Nadu Karnataka Keralam Sports Cricket Football Tennis Other News Nation Assembly Elections 2026 World NRI Entertainment Sholay Tollywood Bollywood Sandalwood Kollywood Mollywood Hollywood Movie Reviews Television Music Theatre OTT Opinion and Editorials DC Comments Columns Videos Business Technology Education Hyderabad Chronicle DC Decaf Featured × Advertisement Home » Tabloid » Hyderabad Chronicle Wash Out, Wipe Out and Chuck Norovirus Hyderabad Chronicle Rochelle Crasto 15 August 2026 2:55 PM15 August 2026 2:55 PM Doctors are seeing a rise in viral stomach infections, especially norovirus-like illnesses that spread rapidly in crowded spaces x It begins quietly. Someone in the office skips lunch because they feel nauseous. A child returns from school complaining of stomach cramps. (DC) Select Deccan Chronicle Now It begins quietly. Someone in the office skips lunch because they feel nauseous. A child returns from school complaining of stomach cramps. A friend cancels dinner plans because of some kind of stomach bug. Within a day or two, the illness seems to spread everywhere — across classrooms, apartment buildings, workplaces, and entire families. Stomach Bugs Doctors are currently noticing a rise in viral stomach infections, especially norovirus-like illnesses that spread rapidly in crowded spaces. Commonly referred to as the “stomach flu” — although it has nothing to do with influenza — norovirus is one of the most contagious stomach infections in the world. Also Read - Secret Behind Those Perfect Hairlines Advertisement The symptoms are unpleasant and often sudden: vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach cramps, nausea, weakness, chills, fever, and body aches that can leave even healthy adults completely exhausted. “It spreads very easily through contaminated hands, food, water, and shared surfaces,” says Dr Manjusha Agarwal, Consultant- Internal Medicine at Gleneagles Hospital Mumbai. Norovirus Spread • Norovirus can spread through contaminated doorknobs, shared washroom surfaces, or even improperly washed hands, and can quickly spread the virus from one person to another. Also Read - South Stars Find a New Base in Mumbai Discover more Political news updates Breaking news alerts Nation news updates • Crowded environments such as schools, offices, restaurants, and shared public spaces make outbreaks much harder to control. • Symptoms are unpleasant and often sudden: vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach cramps, nausea, weakness, chills, fever, and body aches. Break The Chain According to Dr Meghraj Ingle, Senior Consultant Gastroentero-logy at Zen Multispeciality Hospital, the virus can survive on surfaces for long periods if proper cleaning is not done. “Even a tiny amount of the virus can infect someone,” he explains, which is why outbreaks are commonly seen in schools, offices, hospitals, and crowded residential spaces. Also Read - Whey Too Much Protein Fixation Most cases improve within a few days, but doctors say many people underestimate how quickly dehydration can become dangerous. “We are seeing patients wait too long hoping the infection will settle at home,” says Dr Agarwal. “If symptoms do not improve within 12 hours, especially with repeated vomiting or diarrhoea, it is important to contact a doctor.” The biggest concern is dehydration. When the body rapidly loses fluids through vomiting and loose motions, weakness can escalate quickly. In children and elderly individuals, the condition can become serious within hours because their bodies are less able to compensate for fluid loss. Also Read - Fifty-One Years and Counting! Expert Advice Dr Sanjay Nagarkar, Internal Medicine Expert at Apollo Spectra Hospital Pune, says, “Emergency rooms are seeing patients arrive with severe weakness, dizziness, low blood pressure, confusion, and inability to retain fluids.” Some patients require IV fluids and emergency monitoring after prolonged dehydration. Doctors warn that symptoms such as blood in stools, persistent vomiting, fainting, reduced urination, high fever, breathing difficulty, or confusion should never be ignored. One reason many people struggle to identify norovirus early is that it often resembles food poisoning. Food poisoning usually develops within hours after eating contaminated food and often affects multiple people who consumed the same meal. Viral stomach infections, on the other hand, spread from person to person and are more likely to include fever, body aches, fatigue, and nausea alongside digestive symptoms. Be Patient With Recovery Recovery, interestingly, is where many people make mistakes. The moment symptoms slightly improve, people often return to oily food, caffeine, spicy meals, or heavy takeout. Others stop drinking fluids because nausea makes water difficult to tolerate. Some begin taking antibiotics without medical advice, even though norovirus is a viral infection and antibiotics are usually unnecessary. Doctors say simple meals, oral rehydration solutions, electrolyte drinks, coconut water, and proper rest are often the best support for the body while it heals. Returning to work or school too early can also increase the chances of spreading the infection to others. In many ways, norovirus feels like a reminder of how fragile routines can be. One small virus can suddenly slow entire households down — replacing busy schedules with medicine strips, electrolyte sachets, plain khichdi, and long hours of rest. Sometimes healing really is as simple as staying hydrated, staying home, and allowing the body the time it has been asking for all along. Stop The Spread • Handwashing remains one of the strongest protections against norovirus transmission. • Doctors recommend frequent washing with soap and water. • Avoid shared utensils, disinfect frequently touched surfaces, drink clean water, and eat properly cooked food. • If multiple family members fall sick, isolating infected individuals as much as possible and regularly cleaning shared bathrooms and surfaces can help reduce further spread. Someone in the office skips lunch because they feel nauseous. A child returns from school complaining of stomach cramps. (DC) Select Deccan Chronicle Now It begins quietly. Someone in the office skips lunch because they feel nauseous. A child returns from school complaining of stomach cramps. A friend cancels dinner plans because of some kind of stomach bug. Within a day or two, the illness seems to spread everywhere — across classrooms, apartment buildings, workplaces, and entire families. Stomach Bugs Doctors are currently noticing a rise in viral stomach infections, especially norovirus-like illnesses that spread rapidly in crowded spaces. Commonly referred to as the “stomach flu” — although it has nothing to do with influenza — norovirus is one of the most contagious stomach infections in the world. Also Read - Secret Behind Those Perfect Hairlines Advertisement The symptoms are unpleasant and often sudden: vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach cramps, nausea, weakness, chills, fever, and body aches that can leave even healthy adults completely exhausted. “It spreads very easily through contaminated hands, food, water, and shared surfaces,” says Dr Manjusha Agarwal, Consultant- Internal Medicine at Gleneagles Hospital Mumbai. Norovirus Spread • Norovirus can spread through contaminated doorknobs, shared washroom surfaces, or even improperly washed hands, and can quickly spread the virus from one person to another. Also Read - South Stars Find a New Base in Mumbai Discover more Political news updates Breaking news alerts Nation news updates • Crowded environments such as schools, offices, restaurants, and shared public spaces make outbreaks much harder to control. • Symptoms are unpleasant and often sudden: vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach cramps, nausea, weakness, chills, fever, and body aches. Break The Chain According to Dr Meghraj Ingle, Senior Consultant Gastroentero-logy at Zen Multispeciality Hospital, the virus can survive on surfaces for long periods if proper cleaning is not done. “Even a tiny amount of the virus can infect someone,” he explains, which is why outbreaks are commonly seen in schools, offices, hospitals, and crowded residential spaces. Also Read - Whey Too Much Protein Fixation Most cases improve within a few days, but doctors say many people underestimate how quickly dehydration can become dangerous. “We are seeing patients wait too long hoping the infection will settle at home,” says Dr Agarwal. “If symptoms do not improve within 12 hours, especially with repeated vomiting or diarrhoea, it is important to contact a doctor.” The biggest concern is dehydration. When the body rapidly loses fluids through vomiting and loose motions, weakness can escalate quickly. In children and elderly individuals, the condition can become serious within hours because their bodies are less able to compensate for fluid loss. Also Read - Fifty-One Years and Counting! Expert Advice Dr Sanjay Nagarkar, Internal Medicine Expert at Apollo Spectra Hospital Pune, says, “Emergency rooms are seeing patients arrive with severe weakness, dizziness, low blood pressure, confusion, and inability to retain fluids.” Some patients require IV fluids and emergency monitoring after prolonged dehydration. Doctors warn that symptoms such as blood in stools, persistent vomiting, fainting, reduced urination, high fever, breathing difficulty, or confusion should never be ignored. One reason many people struggle to identify norovirus early is that it often resembles food poisoning. Food poisoning usually develops within hours after eating contaminated food and often affects multiple people who consumed the same meal. Viral stomach infections, on the other hand, spread from person to person and are more likely to include fever, body aches, fatigue, and nausea alongside digestive symptoms. Be Patient With Recovery Recovery, interestingly, is where many people make mistakes. The moment symptoms slightly improve, people often return to oily food, caffeine, spicy meals, or heavy takeout. Others stop drinking fluids because nausea makes water difficult to tolerate. Some begin taking antibiotics without medical advice, even though norovirus is a viral infection and antibiotics are usually unnecessary. Doctors say simple meals, oral rehydration solutions, electrolyte drinks, coconut water, and proper rest are often the best support for the body while it heals. Returning to work or school too early can also increase the chances of spreading the infection to others. In many ways, norovirus feels like a reminder of how fragile routines can be. One small virus can suddenly slow entire households down — replacing busy schedules with medicine strips, electrolyte sachets, plain khichdi, and long hours of rest. Sometimes healing really is as simple as staying hydrated, staying home, and allowing the body the time it has been asking for all along. Stop The Spread • Handwashing remains one of the strongest protections against norovirus transmission. • Doctors recommend frequent washing with soap and water. • Avoid shared utensils, disinfect frequently touched surfaces, drink clean water, and eat properly cooked food. • If multiple family members fall sick, isolating infected individuals as much as possible and regularly cleaning shared bathrooms and surfaces can help reduce further spread. news.content_title: 125 people sick in third Princess cruise norovirus outbreak this year
news.content: More than 120 people got sick in a norovirus outbreak aboard a Princess Cruises ship, marking the cruise line’s third this year. Among the 3,032 guests sailing on Ruby Princess, 102 reported being ill, along with 23 crew members, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Their main symptoms were diarrhea and vomiting. The health agency listed the impacted voyage dates as June 12 through July 2. The ship was sailing an Alaska and Canada voyage round-trip from San Francisco, according to CruiseMapper . More: Parasitic infection cases in Michigan explode in 10 days Princess said "a limited number of guests reported mild gastrointestinal illness" during the trip. "Our crew responded promptly by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols across the ship, and cases have since decreased and remain low," the company told USA TODAY in an emailed statement. The cruise line also isolated sick passengers and employees, along with other steps, the CDC said. The ship arrived in San Francisco as planned and "will be undergoing comprehensive cleaning and disinfection" before its next cruise, Princess added. The CDC has logged seven outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships that met its threshold for public notification so far in 2026. Two were due to E. coli, while the rest were caused by norovirus, including two on other Princess ships. There were 23 outbreaks that met that threshold in 2025, 18 of which were caused by norovirus, and the illness was behind 15 out of 18 outbreaks the prior year. While norovirus is frequently associated with cruise ships, those instances account for just 1% of all outbreaks reported . "(Outbreaks are) often taking place within the community, and oftentimes we don't know that they're happening," Sarah R. Michaels, an assistant professor at Tulane University’s Celia Scott Weatherhead School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine, previously told USA TODAY. "Really, when we have these areas where people ... are in really close contact, things like day care facilities, nursing homes and cruise ships, it’s more likely (to be) diagnosed, reported and brought to our attention." This story has been updated to add new information. Nathan Diller is a consumer travel reporter for USA TODAY based in Nashville. You can reach him at ndiller@usatoday.com. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Princess cruise norovirus outbreak sickens hundreds of guests, crew

analysis.time: The outbreak occurred during the voyage dates of June 12 through July 2, 2026, as reported by the CDC (N4). The news was published on August 13, 2026 (N1).
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak took place on the Ruby Princess cruise ship, which was sailing an Alaska and Canada voyage round-trip from San Francisco (N5). Among the 3,032 guests, 102 reported being ill, along with 23 crew members (N2).
analysis.event: A norovirus outbreak sickened 125 people aboard the Princess Cruises ship Ruby Princess, marking the cruise line’s third such incident in 2026 (N1). The CDC confirmed the outbreak, and Princess Cruises stated that a limited number of guests reported mild gastrointestinal illness (N6).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak affected 102 guests and 23 crew members, totaling 125 individuals. The CDC noted that norovirus accounts for just 1% of all outbreaks reported in 2026 (N13).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Princess Cruises implemented enhanced sanitation protocols and isolated sick passengers and employees, as stated by the CDC (N7, N8). The ship arrived in San Francisco as planned and will undergo comprehensive cleaning before its next cruise (N9). The CDC has logged seven outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships that met its threshold for public notification in 2026 (N10).

analysis.brief_en: A norovirus outbreak aboard the Princess Cruises ship Ruby Princess sickened 125 people, including 102 guests and 23 crew members, during its Alaska and Canada voyage from June 12 to July 2, 2026. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed the outbreak, which marks the cruise line’s third such incident in 2026. Princess Cruises responded by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols and isolating affected individuals. The ship arrived in San Francisco as planned and will undergo comprehensive cleaning before its next cruise. The CDC noted that norovirus accounts for just 1% of all outbreaks reported in 2026, highlighting the relatively low prevalence of the virus compared to other pathogens. The outbreak underscores the challenges of managing gastrointestinal illnesses in confined spaces like cruise ships, where close contact increases the risk of transmission.

Photograph: Julian Eales/Alamy The Guide #256: Norovirus, giant puddles, sit-ins and no beer – how can festivals survive the worst? In this week’s newsletter: As promoters like James Scarlett prove, the UK’s festival circuit continues to weather each disaster with remarkable grit Don’t get The Guide delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Running a festival is not for the faint-hearted. The list of potential weekend-derailers is dauntingly long – licensing issues, awol bands, freak weather events to name but a few – and one misstep could prove disastrous, particularly for those smaller non-conglomerate festivals where every last penny and punter counts. Thirty six UK festivals have been cancelled so far in 2026 – and if a festival is cancelled one year, it makes returning for the next one vastly more challenging. The heartening news is that’s the lowest annual figure for cancelled fests since Covid (though admittedly with still some of the season to run), and less than half the number of festivals that were cancelled in 2024. All things considered, the UK and Ireland’s independent festival scene is – like its able-to-survive-in-a-tent-for-four-days-without-a-shower-or-sleep attenders – remarkably hardy. There are success stories all over the place, from Sea Power’s Krankenhaus event in Cumbria, to the mighty End of the Road festival in Wiltshire, which celebrates its 20th instalment this month. Festival promoter James Scarlett is behind two other festival success stories: rock, punk and emo fest 2000 Trees, which enjoyed its 19th outing last month, and the metal, prog and post-rock-tinged ArcTanGent, whose fully sold out 12th edition takes place next week. Because he doesn’t have enough on, James also, along with fellow festival promoter Gavin McInally, hosts Two Promoters One Pod, a podcast entertainingly sharing the challenges of putting on massive great musical shindigs. Last year, to get a sense of those challenges, we asked James to do some festival firefighting and solve some major theoretical doomsday scenarios, and we enjoyed it so much we’ve booked him again this year for an encore set. He’s already ticked off one potential nightmare this year, with 2000 Trees landing in the middle of our never-ending summer heatwave (the forecast for ArcTanGent is looking thankfully cooler, touch wood), but here are five others: Festival disaster #1 | Your costly Friday night headlining band, a huge draw for punters, comes up to you 15 minutes before they are due to go onstage, and say that their fee is insufficient, and they want another 10% on top. What do you do? I think you try to talk to them about how you’re independent and basically a bunch of friends and family running a festival and pulling this sort of thing isn’t going to look good. I do know a festival that this happened to, which I can’t name: they literally got their banking app out and showed the band how much money the festival had to its name. And the band are like, “Oh, OK, we’ll play.” Otherwise, it’s a shitty thing in the extreme to ask that. Festival disaster #2 | Norovirus sweeps through the site, causing mass nausea, vomiting and other unpleasantness. What do you do? [NB. this actually happened at German electronic festival Whole earlier this summer] How can we stop it spreading? Education! To be honest, I’d probably literally be Googling “how do you avoid transmitting norovirus?” These sorts of things, where you’ve never had them happen before, you kind of wing it. We’ve got an onsite app, so can put up notifications, as well as on social media and put signs up about hand-washing and personal contact. Don’t touch anyone! And we’d make sure hand-washing facilities are up to date. We’d be trying to figure out the source, where the outbreak has come from. Is it from inside the festival? The people who you really can’t let get ill are the bands, so maybe quarantining some of them would be needed too. Festival disaster #3 | Two days into your four-day festival, your supplier runs out of beer. What do you do? View image in fullscreen No party without the beer tent. Photograph: Maja Smiejkowska/Shutterstock You usually know if you’re going to run out half a day before. At that point you’re on the phone to the brewery and they’re hopefully bringing more beer to you. But because we want to work with independent businesses, instead of big corporates, there is a limit to how much beer they’ve got. If your brewery runs out, you’ve got a very difficult decision to make as to whether you try to source some other beer. I mean, you could literally drive to a cash and carry, and buy some cans of Carling. But we have a deal in place with our brewery, so we’ve never done that. Last year at 2000 Trees we ran out on Saturday evening, which was really frustrating because you’re leaving money in people’s pockets, without wanting to sound like a corporate beast! But equally you’re like, “well we’ve sold everything so we must have had a good year!” Festival disaster #4 | An activist group begin a mass sit-in in front your main stage and refuse to leave until the festival is finished. What do you do? skip past newsletter promotion after newsletter promotion My unofficial answer is that I’d be down there with my mates trying to get these people out of the way because at the end of the day, you’ve got 15,000 people there for a festival. I’m all about the right to protest but if you’re disrupting my ability to put food on the table for my family and pay my mortgage, I start to feel a bit different about things. We’ve had something like this happen at 2000 Trees, when we booked Drag Queen Story Hour. Some far-right zealots must have search terms set up, so when the words “drag queen” come up on Facebook they get alerted and go and protest it. They started sending us loads of hate messages, saying that they were going to come in buses, and blockade the road. But those people are cowards. They’re just 45-year-old men sat behind the computer in their mum’s spare room. They’ve got a lot of hate, but nothing to back it up. So it never went anywhere – and we put on Drag Queen Story Hour the following year too. Festival disaster #5 | A huge storm on the first night of the festival causes major disruption, with standing water in much of the campsite and on several of the stages. What do you do? We’ve sucked puddles out before. I mean, how much water you can suck out, is debateable, but don’t forget, you’ve got a toilet contractor on site who is sucking waste out of toilets all weekend. So they have suckers! It would depend how much water there was. Water creates a drowning risk and doesn’t go well with electricity. You have to make sure there’s no power anywhere near it. I think it’s important to get a site with good drainage. Here at ArcTanGent, the site’s on limestone cliffs. So actually, the water does have somewhere to go, because limestone is porous. But on other sites the water doesn’t have anywhere to go. I remember seeing a video of Creamfields one year. And it was like a flash flood in the campsite and there was a raging river going through the campsite. I mean, that’s a life and death thing. You’ve got to be really careful. He’s already ticked off one potential nightmare this year, with 2000 Trees landing in the middle of our never-ending summer heatwave (the forecast for ArcTanGent is looking thankfully cooler, touch wood), but here are five others: Festival disaster #1 | Your costly Friday night headlining band, a huge draw for punters, comes up to you 15 minutes before they are due to go onstage, and say that their fee is insufficient, and they want another 10% on top. What do you do? I think you try to talk to them about how you’re independent and basically a bunch of friends and family running a festival and pulling this sort of thing isn’t going to look good. I do know a festival that this happened to, which I can’t name: they literally got their banking app out and showed the band how much money the festival had to its name. And the band are like, “Oh, OK, we’ll play.” Otherwise, it’s a shitty thing in the extreme to ask that. Festival disaster #2 | Norovirus sweeps through the site, causing mass nausea, vomiting and other unpleasantness. What do you do? [NB. this actually happened at German electronic festival Whole earlier this summer] How can we stop it spreading? Education! To be honest, I’d probably literally be Googling “how do you avoid transmitting norovirus?” These sorts of things, where you’ve never had them happen before, you kind of wing it. We’ve got an onsite app, so can put up notifications, as well as on social media and put signs up about hand-washing and personal contact. Don’t touch anyone! And we’d make sure hand-washing facilities are up to date. We’d be trying to figure out the source, where the outbreak has come from. Is it from inside the festival? The people who you really can’t let get ill are the bands, so maybe quarantining some of them would be needed too. Festival disaster #3 | Two days into your four-day festival, your supplier runs out of beer. What do you do? View image in fullscreen No party without the beer tent. Photograph: Maja Smiejkowska/Shutterstock You usually know if you’re going to run out half a day before. At that point you’re on the phone to the brewery and they’re hopefully bringing more beer to you. But because we want to work with independent businesses, instead of big corporates, there is a limit to how much beer they’ve got. If your brewery runs out, you’ve got a very difficult decision to make as to whether you try to source some other beer. I mean, you could literally drive to a cash and carry, and buy some cans of Carling. But we have a deal in place with our brewery, so we’ve never done that. Last year at 2000 Trees we ran out on Saturday evening, which was really frustrating because you’re leaving money in people’s pockets, without wanting to sound like a corporate beast! But equally you’re like, “well we’ve sold everything so we must have had a good year!” Festival disaster #4 | An activist group begin a mass sit-in in front your main stage and refuse to leave until the festival is finished. What do you do? skip past newsletter promotion after newsletter promotion My unofficial answer is that I’d be down there with my mates trying to get these people out of the way because at the end of the day, you’ve got 15,000 people there for a festival. I’m all about the right to protest but if you’re disrupting my ability to put food on the table for my family and pay my mortgage, I start to feel a bit different about things. We’ve had something like this happen at 2000 Trees, when we booked Drag Queen Story Hour. Some far-right zealots must have search terms set up, so when the words “drag queen” come up on Facebook they get alerted and go and protest it. They started sending us loads of hate messages, saying that they were going to come in buses, and blockade the road. But those people are cowards. They’re just 45-year-old men sat behind the computer in their mum’s spare room. They’ve got a lot of hate, but nothing to back it up. So it never went anywhere – and we put on Drag Queen Story Hour the following year too. Festival disaster #5 | A huge storm on the first night of the festival causes major disruption, with standing water in much of the campsite and on several of the stages. What do you do? We’ve sucked puddles out before. I mean, how much water you can suck out, is debateable, but don’t forget, you’ve got a toilet contractor on site who is sucking waste out of toilets all weekend. So they have suckers! It would depend how much water there was. Water creates a drowning risk and doesn’t go well with electricity. You have to make sure there’s no power anywhere near it. I think it’s important to get a site with good drainage. Here at ArcTanGent, the site’s on limestone cliffs. So actually, the water does have somewhere to go, because limestone is porous. But on other sites the water doesn’t have anywhere to go. I remember seeing a video of Creamfields one year. And it was like a flash flood in the campsite and there was a raging river going through the campsite. I mean, that’s a life and death thing. You’ve got to be really careful.
